executiveSummary: GM0397's 2025 identity, population, neighbourhood, place and safety-region inputs reconcile, and the focused deterministic gate passes all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. Release nevertheless remains correction-required. The coastal preset reports an internal flood field of 2.109798 and 16,860 affected people-equivalent at T+24 without a selected North Sea/Rijnland-boezem/Ringvaart event, defence or breach state, connected footprint, arrival or recession. The exact-zero named-major-river result is valid only as a narrow Rhine/Meuse/IJssel screen and is not an all-clear for the Ringvaart, Spaarne, Leidsevaart, regional kades, polders, sewers or pluvial flow. Seven unrelated hazards reuse exactly the same complete fourteen-neighbourhood rank. A controlled T+11 fire source inside De Glip near Wandelbos Groenendaal ranks the source neighbourhood only seventh while Heemsteedse Dreef leads. The logical mobility graph contains only the eastbound N201 connection to Haarlemmermeer and omits the same N201 corridor westward plus N208/Haarlem/Bloemendaal continuity documented by official sources. Public water-control, wastewater, road, rail, care, education, antenna and grid-planning records improve context but do not establish live topology, capacity, backup or recovery. Unknown and NoData must never be rendered as zero or safe, and every precise first-72-hour effect must remain a transparent exercise output until governed event-valid evidence supports it.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM0397 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood and place geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; PDOK services inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0397 as Heemstede and reports 27,638 residents, density 3,013/km², 28.1% aged 65 or older and 4,516 one-person households; the generated municipality centre is inside the 2025 boundary.

Fourteen published neighbourhood rows sum to 27,630 residents, eight below the municipality total (-0.029%); households sum to 12,285 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 7,785. Deterministic allocation reconciles to 27,638 without rewriting source rows.

One active BAG woonplaats and one BRT woonkern are named Heemstede. BAG/PDOK place context is Public Domain Mark 1.0 and updated independently from the annual generalized CBS polygons; labels are not flood compartments, sewer catchments, service areas or present-person footprints.

CBS null, suppressed, unavailable and not-applicable values remain NoData. Annual registered residents exclude commuters, rail passengers, care visitors, pupils, responders and recreational visitors and therefore cannot be interpreted as event-time occupancy.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel Kennemerland 2023-2030 and current crisis-type pages
supports: The official profile includes Heemstede among the nine municipalities and evaluates flooding, nature fire, extreme weather, electricity/gas/drinking-water/ICT interruption, land/water/rail/tunnel incidents, vulnerable objects, health threats and reception of large groups.

VRK says flood impact depends on breach location and size, flow velocity and ground elevation and can cascade to vital infrastructure. That supports explicit scenario selection, not a municipality-centre distance scalar.

The profile describes 80 km² of regional forest/dune, drought-sensitive fire development, difficult access, threat to homes and care institutions, smoke and potentially large evacuation. It also identifies N200/N201 coastal traffic through the Zandvoort-Bloemendaal-Haarlem-Heemstede corridor as affecting emergency access.

This is official multi-year qualitative planning context, not a live warning, incident, resource inventory, probability, evacuation decision, route state or restoration commitment. No standard open-data licence or machine update cadence was found for the narrative pages.

evidenceSources.title: Klimaatadaptatie measures and local climate-risk policy
evidenceSources.edition: Current public page inspected 3 September 2026; strategic cooperation cites 2019 stress test and planned 2025 update
supports: The municipality explicitly recognizes heavy rain, flooding, drought, heat and forest-fire consequences and is implementing separated storm-water collection, infiltration/drainage, extra surface storage, shade and de-paving.

The 2024-2027 strategic cooperation agreement with Rijnland says Heemstede's 2019 climate stress test covered extreme precipitation, heat, drought and flooding and was planned for update in 2025. A planning statement or planned refresh is not proof that a current machine-readable layer is complete or operational.

The page offers address-level advice through a climate map but does not state a reusable API, native raster resolution, fixed refresh cadence, complete NoData encoding or blanket redistribution licence. Until those are verified, its content is dated context only and missing areas remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: Vernieuwing riool Lindenlaan en omgeving
evidenceSources.edition: Project status March 2026; realization planned from 2027
supports: Municipal tests identify streets between Binnenweg, Esdoornkade, Blekersvaart and Lindenlaan, plus Kastanjelaan, Dr. Droogplein, Berkenlaan, Eikenlaan and Haemstedelaan, as sensitive to water nuisance and heat stress; the local sewer is stated to be 93 years old and due for replacement.

The page separates preparation/design in 2025-2026 from realization beginning in 2027. Project-valid time must therefore be retained and proposed renewal must not be represented as completed protection.

The page provides site-specific official evidence but no event-time sewer surcharge, catchment topology, inlet/culvert state, pump availability, depth surface, capacity units, backup or restoration. It cannot validate the simulator's exact local water or drainage values.

evidenceSources.title: Rijnland water-overload operations, drought measures and Heemstede wastewater connection
evidenceSources.edition: Current pages and 2026 operational timeline inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Rijnland describes event-dependent pre-drawdown, full-capacity pumping, controlled emergency-pump deployment, peak storage, monitoring and kade inspection. These actions require time-stamped confirmation and cannot be inferred from a generic preparedness setting.

The 2026 drought timeline records a temporary salinity-control barrier in the Leidsevaart at Kohnstammlaan, Heemstede, changing navigation between route nodes, and later records its removal. This demonstrates dynamically coupled water-quality, water-level and mobility state while also showing why a dated action must not be applied outside its validity window.

Rijnland's Zwanenburg treatment project documents two wastewater transport pipes from pumping stations in Haarlem-Schalkwijk and Heemstede, crossing beneath the Ringvaart, with sludge routed toward Haarlem Waarderpolder. It establishes a cross-boundary wastewater dependency, not current flow, spare capacity, power backup or failover.
Rijnland registers and operational pages do not publish all live controls, connected catchments or restoration commitments under a fixed reusable machine contract; missing state is Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Dutch water boards; Rijkswaterstaat/WMCN
evidenceSources.title: IMWA/DAMO water assets and LIWO flood-scenario catalogue
evidenceSources.edition: HWH deployment snapshot 3 September 2026; LIWO release 2025.1.6
supports: The CC BY-SA 4.0 HWH snapshot assigns fourteen point assets to GM0397 by full CBS boundary containment: one DWA/RWA sewer pump and thirteen surface-water pumps, including named flushing, underdrainage, Heemstederveld and Groenendaal records. Contributor completeness varies.

A registered or realized point does not prove hydraulic connectivity, flow direction, compatible capacity units, telemetry, current operation, power/backup, condition, crews or restoration. Null capacity remains Unknown and assets do not affect the current simulation.

LIWO 2025.1.6 exposes candidate primary, regional, regional-water-system and outside-dike breach locations plus expert scenario products. A marker or available tile is not a selected Heemstede event, live breach, probability or forecast.

Any causal adapter must preserve catalogue release, scenario/model date, source water, defence/breach and variant, depth/velocity/arrival/duration, native CRS/resolution/units, coverage, NoData, licence and exercise approval; otherwise local depth and service effects remain unsupported.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Province of Noord-Holland / ProRail / OVapi / NDW
evidenceSources.title: NWB roads, N201/N208 and Cruquiusbrug, rail, scheduled transit and current road context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; provincial pages current 3 September 2026; GTFS version 9543; public context retrieved 2-3 September 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB currently produces only one GM0397 logical link: N201 east to Haarlemmermeer, nominally 150 scenario units. The municipality and province separately document N201 continuing from Zandvoort via Heemstede to Hoofddorp and the N208/N201 junction at Herenweg-Zandvoortselaan, so degree one is not a complete emergency-access representation.

The province says the two movable Cruquiusbrug structures carry the N201 across the Ringvaart; the renovation completed in March/April 2026. Dated closures and a May 2026 operating fault separately affected road modes, buses, emergency routing and navigation, proving mode- and time-specific state rather than a permanent capacity.

ProRail's manually updated CC0 register identifies Heemstede-Aerdenhout station, and GTFS version 9543 contains 34 stop areas. Static geometry and schedules do not establish passenger presence, event-time service, capacity, accessibility, evacuation throughput or restoration.

The CC0 NDW snapshot assigns zero covered current road situations to GM0397. Zero matching reports means no covered record at publication time, never that N201/N208, Cruquiusbrug, local streets, rail or crossings are open.

evidenceSources.publisher: Netbeheer Nederland / Partners in Energie; RDI; RIVM; DUO
evidenceSources.title: Electricity planning sample, antenna register, acute-care questionnaire and education locations
evidenceSources.edition: Public deployment snapshots retrieved 2-3 September 2026; RIVM acute care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: One-postcode sampling identifies Stedin service-area planning context for Heemstede with 27 projects and earliest project year 2026. Capacity/projects are updated at least quarterly and queues monthly, but the exact dataset licence identifier was not found. A sample and congestion class are not full coverage, topology, live load, outage or restoration.

RDI's public WFS assigns 33 antenna-installation records to GM0397: fourteen mobile-communication, seven fixed-link, one other-mobile and eleven radio-amateur sites. Service cadence and reuse licence are unstated; point records do not establish coverage, traffic, ownership, backhaul, power/backup, availability or recovery.

RIVM's national 2026 hospital questionnaire is CC0 and assigns no acute-care location inside GM0397. This means no covered respondent location intersects the boundary, not that care need is zero; patient transfer and acceptance at Haarlem/Hoofddorp remain event-time Unknowns.

DUO's daily CC-BY register assigns seventeen education-use locations. Registered use does not establish present pupils, shelter designation, accessibility, occupancy, stocks, generator endurance or live operating status. All four source families remain official context with affectsSimulation=false.

Official water, transport, antenna, care, education and grid-planning records remain affectsSimulation=false. Their presence is not silently treated as live state, and their absence is not proof of safety.

findings.summary: Generic coastal proximity becomes precise local flood and service impact without a selected Rijnland/LIWO hydraulic event.
findings.evidence: At coastal T+24 the model reports internal flood field 2.109798, critical status, 16,860 affected people-equivalent and drainage availability 0.254951. E02/E05/E06 require source water, breach/defence state, flow, terrain and connected footprint; none is selected. The direct river result is exactly zero only because the preset screens Rhine/Meuse/IJssel, not Ringvaart, Spaarne, Leidsevaart, boezem, regional kades or polders.
findings.action: Retain coastal proximity solely as a hidden non-operational diagnostic and suppress decision-facing depth, local affected people and direct service loss until an expert-selected, versioned LIWO/Rijnland event carries source water, defence/breach/variant, native depth/velocity/arrival/duration, CRS/resolution/units/NoData, uncertainty and approval. Retain river zero as a narrowly labelled named-major-river result, never a local-water all-clear.

findings.summary: Named municipal drainage sensitivity and changing sewer state do not drive pluvial depth or priority.
findings.evidence: E03/E04 identify separated systems, infiltration/storage measures and specific water/heat-sensitive streets around Lindenlaan/Binnenweg/Blekersvaart, with the 93-year-old sewer still in design and realization planned from 2027. E05/E06 identify dynamic Rijnland controls and fourteen partial asset points. The model instead reports T+24 flood field 0.855202 and 10,338 affected using a generic curve and shared neighbourhood seed without rain-grid selection, terrain, paving, inlet/culvert, sewer catchment/capacity, receiving-water or project-valid state.
findings.action: Ingest an authority-approved versioned climate-stress/sewer-catchment surface with precipitation event, AHN terrain, paving, drainage direction, inlet/culvert/pump assumptions, project-valid state, units, uncertainty, coverage and NoData. Until available, expose named sites as dated context and keep numeric local pluvial allocation unsupported.

findings.summary: Seven unrelated hazards reuse one complete fourteen-neighbourhood ordering.
findings.evidence: At T+24 storm, pluvial, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire have the identical descending order led by Heemsteedse Dreef, Rivierenbuurt and Schouwbroekerpolder and ending with Glipper Dreef. E02-E06 distinguish drainage, flood, heat, fire, target and access mechanisms; their editions do not validate current event intensity but falsify the claim that one shared seeded rank represents each mechanism.
findings.action: Replace the shared seed with hazard-specific versioned surfaces and eligibility, source/perimeter/flow geometry, valid time, uncertainty and NoData. Add regressions requiring materially different flood, heat, fire, wind/winter and cyber ranks and explicit Unknown local cells when evidence is unavailable.

findings.summary: A controlled Groenendaal-area fire does not prioritize its source neighbourhood.

De Glip ranks 7/14 while Heemsteedse Dreef ranks first. E02 describes source/fuel/weather/access/smoke dynamics; E03 and municipal woodland context do not establish current fuel or an incident.
findings.action: Use IPO/Risicokaart combustible nature and BRT land cover only as dated eligibility, then require source/perimeter, fuel/moisture, wind, paths/access, extinguishing water and suppression state for causal spread. Add source-cell ranking/containment tests. Keep the focused source synthetic and canonical remote wildfire's zero local flame distinct from local fire planning.

findings.action: Rebuild boundary lifelines from monthly NWB junction geometry and audit N201 west/east and N208 north/south continuation. Add typed, non-additive road, bridge/navigation, rail, bus, cycling/pedestrian and patient-transfer edges with open/restricted/closed/Unknown validity. findings.action: Mark all nine local hazard families unsupported until a governed event is selected. Require valid-time KNMI observations/warnings or exercise forcing for weather, a named seismic event/ShakeMap and local response for earthquake replay, and named targets/attack/containment for cyber. Preserve mechanism-specific Unknown, indirect and remote-effects states.

Recovery requires hydraulic recession/dewatering and operator confirmation/range; a generic response multiplier must never appear as a completed action or promise.

Show publisher, edition, issue/valid/retrieval time, unit, coverage, licence, confidence and affectsSimulation adjacent to local outputs. Add tests that null capacity never becomes zero, planned works never become existing protection and river zero never implies all-water safety.

residualLimitations: This is a deterministic first-72-hour planning stress test, not a KNMI, WMCN/LIWO, Rijnland, VRK, province, municipality or operator warning, forecast, probability, evacuation order, casualty model or restoration commitment.

No expert-selected Heemstede coastal/Rijnland-boezem/Ringvaart event, defence/breach/overtopping state, connected footprint, arrival, velocity, duration/recession, verified depth units or NoData mask drives the simulation.

The exact-zero major-river result applies only to direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel forcing; local boezem, Spaarne, Leidsevaart, Ringvaart, regional-kade, polder, groundwater, sewer and pluvial risk remains Unknown.

The municipal climate page, 2019 stress-test reference and Lindenlaan project are dated planning context; they do not provide a verified current reusable raster, event-time depth or completed 2027 sewer protection.

CBS generalized municipality/neighbourhood polygons and label points do not resolve terrain, water compartments, sewer catchments, buildings, paving, shade, fuel, care sites, corridors or household exposure.
CBS neighbourhood values are rounded/suppressed; district-heating, charging and one cars-per-household value remain null. Null is Unknown, never zero service, zero demand or safe.
Registered residents exclude commuters, station passengers, pupils, care visitors, responders and recreational visitors; no authorized event-time transient occupancy ledger is available.

IPO/Risicokaart/BRT forest polygons would be static eligibility only; the focused De Glip source is synthetic and no live fuel, moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind, access, extinguishing-water or suppression state is available.
Static NWB, ProRail and GTFS geometry/schedules do not establish live N201/N208/Cruquiusbrug, rail, bus, walking/cycling, evacuation, emergency-priority or freight status and capacity.
Zero covered NDW situations is no covered report at publication time, not proof that roads and bridges are open; dated 2026 Cruquiusbrug states must not be extrapolated.
IMWA/DAMO asset points and Rijnland project pages do not establish full hydraulic/wastewater connectivity, compatible capacity units, control logic, current operation, power backup, crews or repair.

No complete public physical Stedin feeder/switching, potable-water pipe/pressure/quality, gas district/valve, telecom backhaul or municipal sewer topology is authorized in the model; the NBNL postcode sample is planning context only.

No acute-care respondent inside GM0397 is a coverage fact, not zero health-care need; live hospital acceptance, care-home occupancy, staffing, medicines, generators and patient-transfer availability remain Unknown.
Education and antenna registers identify installations/use, not shelter activation, people present, radio coverage, backhaul, capacity, power backup or restoration.
Cyber disruption has no named target, architecture, attack/detection/containment state or authoritative operational evidence; generic service loss is not an observed incident.
No validated inventory is available for shelters/reception, pumps/generators, fuel, food/water/medicine stocks, crews, vehicles, mutual aid, household preparedness or completed actions.

Event-attributable essential-service person-hours is a matched-no-event weighted availability proxy, not customer outage-hours, injuries, mortality, evacuation, displacement or welfare loss; 72 hours excludes prolonged contamination and reconstruction.
